title: Synthetic slope soak harness for autoscale regression smoke tests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a reproducible, low-noise harness that simulates a realistic ramp-to-plateau traffic pattern (a 'slope' soak) with occasional controlled micro-bursts. The goal is to surface regressions in autoscaler responsiveness and p95 latency drift for Dedicated GPU pools while exercising KV cache priming and kernel-selection fallbacks. This ticket scopes building the harness, integrating it with our telemetry pipeline, and adding automated regression checks against a stored baseline.

Scope: build a configurable harness that can: 1) generate a linear ramp (tokens/sec) from a low baseline to N% of pool capacity over configurable duration (10m-120m), 2) dwell at plateau for configurable soak time (30m-6h), 3) inject micro-bursts with jitter and controlled concurrency spikes, 4) include pre-priming phase to warm KV cache and populate prefix caches, 5) record detailed per-request metrics (tokens_in/tokens_out, model_variant, kernel_path, kv_hit, queue_time, service_latency), and 6) run automated regression detection against baseline using both p95 comparisons and distribution-level tests (EWMA of p95 and Kolmogorov-Smirnov on latency histograms).

Non-goals: full A/B rollout automation, dedicated UI; those are follow-ups.

Architectural notes: The harness is implemented as a lightweight Go binary that orchestrates request generators (goroutine pools) and drives our existing request-simulator library. Load scheduling uses a piecewise-linear generator with optional Poisson jitter. Telemetry is exported to Prometheus + Tempo traces and forwarded to the Console staging pipeline (metrics prefix: test.slope_soak.*). The harness writes a JSON run manifest to GCS for later replay and regression analysis.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Harness can run a 60-minute slope (0->70% tokens/sec) + 2h soak + 10x micro-bursts schedule without manual intervention.
- Console shows test.slope_soak.* metrics and a prebuilt dashboard template.
- Regression detection alerts if p95 increases >10% relative to baseline or if KS test p-value < 0.01 between baseline and current latency distributions.
- A CI job can execute a smoke variant in <30m to validate changes in autoscaler codepaths.

Telemetry & thresholds: tokens/sec aggregate, per-model tokens/sec split, p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail error rate, queue_time, autoscaler scaling events (scale_up/down timestamps), capacity utilization. Alert thresholds: p95 > baseline * 1.10 -> create regression finding. Sustained token/sec drop >15% with no scaling activity -> identify routing/backpressure issue.

Data handling: test traffic must use synthetic tenant and not leak customer data. KV cache priming uses synthetic prompts that exercise KV keys; priming phase is optional toggle.

Deliverables: harness binary + Helm job manifests for Dedicated staging, Console dashboard, regression-detection script, CI smoke job, run manifest spec, example run artifacts, postmortem template for failed runs.
plan_steps: Draft ramp-and-burst schedule templates and parameterize durations/targets
Implement piecewise-linear load generator and Poisson jitter wrapper in request-simulator
Add KV cache priming step and flag to toggle priming
Instrument and export detailed metrics to test.slope_soak.* in Prometheus format
Add Tempo tracing spans for kernel selection and kv access path; ensure sample rate is configurable
Create Console dashboard template and a saved query for p95-delta and KS-test visualizations
Implement regression detector that compares run artifact to baseline: EWMA on p95 and KS-test on latency histogram
Create a short CI smoke job that runs a 20-minute slope to 40% + 10m soak for quick verification
Run three full-length validation runs on staging Dedicated pools and collect artifacts
Iterate on thresholds and false-positive tuning based on observed variance
success_criteria: Console dashboard shows consistent metric names and clean labels for all runs
Regression detector triggers for intentional regressions (test fault injection) and remains quiet for stable runs
CI smoke job completes reliably within 30 minutes and reports pass/fail to GitHub PR status
Run manifests and artifacts are stored in gs://redwood-inference-test-artifacts/slope-soak/ and accessible to SRE and MLE teams
results: 2026-03-02: initial harness prototype implemented. Piecewise-linear generator validated locally (k=100 tps to 6000 tps over 30m).

2026-03-04: first staging run (1h ramp to 65% + 90m soak) completed. Observed p95 drift ~12% during ramp window; correlated with a kernel fallback event for quantized model_variant vq4->fp16. Logged traces show additional 15-25ms per-token scheduling delay on fallback nodes.

2026-03-06: mitigations tested: pinned kernel selection and temporary increase in batch size. Re-run reduced p95 drift to ~4% but increased tail CPU utilization. Trade-off noted in run artifact: cpu/mem trends stored with run manifest.
2026-03-09: added KS-test implementation for distribution-level detection. Baseline created from three stable runs (2026-02-26 -> 2026-03-01).

2026-03-10: CI smoke job definition merged into github.com/redwood-inference/pr/1342. Smoke job ran successfully in staging but flagged a false-positive on one run because micro-burst timing overlapped with nightly maintenance window; added blackout-window parameter to harness.
